guardrail_cases.answer: A corporation is a company or group of people authorized to act as a single entity (legally a person) and recognized as such in law. Early incorporated entities were established by charter. A corporation is incorporated in a specific nation and governed by the laws of incorporation in that state. It may issue stock, either private or public, or may be classified as a non-stock corporation.  If stock is issued, the corporation will usually be governed by its shareholders, either directly or indirectly.  A government-owned corporation is engaged in a profit-making enterprise that may require the exercise of powers unique to government.
